-

This is for the sitcom years. 

This is for the early days. Long chats in Taylor's apartment where we realized that we might just be friends over girl dinners from the Bangladeshi bodega on the corner of Nostrand and Halsey.

This is for the early nights ... when we cycled through le bain, the jane, and soho parties before we realized that we actually just like a corner dive ... or even better: em's kombucha on the stoop.

This is for dancing like we were at le bain ... while being at the corner dive.

This is for the hours long chats cuddled in bed talking about pap smears, career spirals, and where to get dim sum the next morning.

This is for the all afternoon walks transporting us through the multiverses of brooklyn neighborhoods. The coffees stops, photo snaps, dog pets and sidewalk stoops.

This is for the prospect park days of lounge, frisbee, snack, yap, on endless rotation.

This is for alllllllll the perfect friends, friends of friends, and friends of friends of friends that we have met and folded in along the way that expanded, brightened, and made life all the way more sweet.

This is for the dreams that turned into realities. The berlin apartment swap, working F1 pitlanes, launching the brand, and following a hunch about european farming.

This is for seeing the most expansive versions of each other, even when it was far from our own imaginations. For the timely reminders that we are capable and worthy of that vision.

This is for the girls that turned to friends that turned to roommates that turned to sisters as we navigated this silly little piece of nyc life.

This is for the sitcom years.

As we wrap 2025, there is so much to be grateful for at birdhouse. 

First and foremost, to our Safekeepers: thank you for creating environments that activate curiosity, honor the child, and keep our classrooms alive. ✨ Learning here often feels like a game of improv - the practice of “yes-anding” children’s ideas and following them into the depths of their curiosity. We see them. And we recommit to seeing them every single day.

To our families: the culture of birdhouse was never predetermined. It has been built day over day with the children and the families who bring their rituals, values, and engagement into our School Family. We are lucky to call you our partners in this work.

And to our birdies 🐣 whose curiosity is boundless, who show up bravely each day with big ideas and big feelings, courageous enough to let us in.

This year was shaped by many moments:

🛶child-led investigations like our Boat Study, where we explored floating, sinking, building, revising, and collaborating

 🎶morning songs that set the tone and ensure every child is seen

🚕 outdoor time exploring the sounds and elements of Brooklyn

🧘yoga and mindfulness, building body awareness and emotional regulation

⛑️ a visit from our local fire station, sparked by the children’s curiosity

🐱gentle, patient care with Khaleesi, our school cat 🐾

🤝 Family Education Night, where we slow down and build community together

And above all, the quieter moments you could miss if you don’t pay attention - the big emotions, the gut belly laughs, two new friends holding hands, the tenderness of an older child helping a younger child zip their jacket, the intrinsic joy when a child builds upon a new skill. These are the ones we live for. 

As we head into 2026, we’re deeply grateful for this community and excited for what’s ahead ✨

It started with a hug… or was it fashion? Hard to tell in Copenhagen — the line is beautifully blurred.
Four impossibly stylish humans gathered around a table @1hotelcopenhagen , dressed like a mood board that got a PhD. I was instantly transfixed. One stood out — leader of the gang? Oracle? Just outrageously well dressed? Whatever it was, pen and watercolours came out.
I sketched fast. Then — poof — they vanished. A hug for the server, coats on, gone into the city.
Usually, that’s enough. A moment caught. Page turned. But this one wouldn’t sit still.
So I asked the server. Turns out: they own a tailor shop around the corner. “Really nice people,” she said. “Warm. I love them.”
Naturally, we went. There they were @herrernesmagasin — full haberdashery glory — fitting gentlemen to the highest standard… and welcoming us with a hot toddy because of course they did.
Summoning courage, I offered the sketch. “F*** me, Allan — come here quickly!” Laughter. Connection. Art doing its quiet magic.
He accepted the portrait. I left with a neck scarf. An exchange not just of creativity, but of humanity.
It ended the best way these things should: a great big hug between two new friends.

Possibly the most Danish man ever 🇩🇰

When you’re in Copenhagen, the Scandinavian look is everywhere — tall, sharp features, stylish glasses, and that effortless I woke up like this way of being. On this day, in this restaurant, this man felt like a national symbol.

So out came the pen and watercolours.
I sketched as he moved through conversations with ease and levity — calm, confident, quietly iconic.

I’ll never meet him again, I’m sure.
But in my mind he lives on forever…
perhaps as the CEO of LEGO, or some other great Scandinavian institution.
Either way, a legend was immortalised.

It was a tremendous honor to attend the New York City Department of Correction Emerald Society Holiday Party and celebrate the proud traditions, service, and dedication of our correction officers. This event was not just a holiday gathering it was a meaningful occasion to recognize the courage, professionalism, and commitment of those who work tirelessly to maintain safety and security in our city. It’s been 10 years and we are still here in an industry where 80% of businesses fail within 5 years.  Even in our own building, One Fulton Square, few have been in this spot since the beginning. Kudos to The Coop for opening before us and continuing to thrive.  After ten years, this little rooftop cocktail bar still lives to do business another day. We’re still here with Yoyo, our head bartender turned general manager, at the helm now. 

The feminine Yin  energy runs strong and proud at Leaf.  A glance at our roster will tell you that.  In alphabetical order:  Deanne, Emma, Esther, Hawa, Jennifer, Jennifer, Michelle, Mikayla, Nicole, Sangye, Vivian.  And let’s not forget the male Yang energy whose duty we acknowledge is to steadfastly and quietly support the Yin energy: Alex, Anibal, Gaspar, Ian, Jeff, Marcos and Saul. 

Let’s raise a glass of one of our first cocktails that has survived the test of time - The Hellcat. We toast the past 10 years of life and welcome the next 10 years of life.
